evidence: accessTokenLogin/accessTokenLoginGet hand the work to authService.validateAnonymousLogin and only turn errors into an HttpException with status FORBIDDEN
The webauthn endpoints (generateAuthenticationOptions, verifyAttestation, verifyAuthentication) pass straight through to webAuthService
googleLoginCallback/oidcLoginCallback only read request.user.jwt and call response.redirect, which is HTTP transport work
oidcLogin blocks the endpoint with a feature-flag check against configurationService, which is endpoint access control
parsedVerdict.reasoning: AuthController does presentation work only. It declares HTTP routes, attaches guards (passport AuthGuard, HasPermissionGuard), reads request bodies and params, and passes the real work to AuthService and WebAuthService. It turns service errors into HTTP 403 responses and sends OAuth callbacks to a frontend URL. Building that redirect URL from ROOT_URL and the language code is transport or routing work, not a business rule. The ENABLE_FEATURE_AUTH_OIDC check in oidcLogin is a feature flag that blocks an endpoint, which is also an ordinary transport-level concern. Login validation, WebAuthn verification and token issuing all happen in the services. The file has no persistence code and no domain logic.
